# Trump's nuclear deal with Saudis jettisons longstanding US demands

![](https://static.files.bbci.co.uk/bbcdotcom/web/20260722-075153-e7d2bae31f-web-3.15.0-4/grey-placeholder.png)
![EPA Trump leads Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman on a tour of the White House in Washington DC last November](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/news/480/cpsprodpb/d2ea/live/84946360-867c-11f1-b60e-a7e0943a9c78.jpg.webp)

The Trump administration's nuclear agreement with Saudi Arabia reversed a years-long stance toward a key Middle East ally.

Past US presidents insisted that Saudi Arabia normalise relations with Israel in exchange for receiving American nuclear technology for civilian energy programmes.

President Donald Trump gave Saudi Arabia what it wanted without extracting concessions for Israel in return - and over objections from critics who argued that it could spark a nuclear arms race in the region.

The deal was the latest example of Trump jettisoning the traditional American approach to the Middle East, which centred on Israel and finding a two-state solution to the Israeli-Palestinian conflict.

In his second term Trump has focused primarily on strengthening America's economic influence to compete with China and other rivals. Analysts said the nuclear pact with Saudi Arabia sent a signal that the US wants to keep regional allies in the fold even if it means angering Israel in the process.

# Houthis claim attack on oil tankers as US launches more strikes on Iran

![](https://static.files.bbci.co.uk/bbcdotcom/web/20260714-093448-684066af18-web-3.14.0-3/grey-placeholder.png)
![Reuters The Bab al-Mandab Strait in an aerial image.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/news/480/cpsprodpb/5df9/live/bacada70-862e-11f1-b1b6-99ee8edc68f7.jpg.webp)

Yemen's Houthis say they have attacked two Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea as the US launched its 12th consecutive night of strikes on Iran.

Iranian state media said two people had been killed in the US strikes on Wednesday, and a tanker caught fire in an explosion in a mined route in the Strait of Hormuz.

Ahead of the latest round of strikes, US President Donald Trump had threatened to destroy an Iranian bridge or power plant if Iran attacked a ship in the strait and to "take care of" the Houthis if they blocked the Red Sea.

If confirmed, the Houthi attack would be the first since the Iran-backed group announced a "maritime embargo" against Saudi Arabia.

The Houthis named the tankers as the Encelia and the Layla, though neither their responsibility, nor the attack on the Layla has been confirmed.

The group's military spokesperson Yahya Saree said they had targeted the ships with drones and missiles for allegedly violating its naval blockade.

Saree added that the Houthis promised to continue their naval operations and would continue "enforcing the 'siege for a siege' equation".

# EU wheat prices fall after Morocco increases duty on Black Sea products

Posted to [Maritime Reporter](/blogs/blogs-maritime_reporter)
on
July 23, 2026

European wheat prices fell on Thursday, after reaching contract highs in the previous session. Traders assessed Morocco's decision to extend its import duties as well as the current situation?in?the Black Sea following attacks by Russia and Ukraine.

The price of front-month 'September milling wheat, traded on the Paris-based Euronext exchange, fell 0.8% to EUR242.5 ($275.84), after earlier trading reached EUR245.75. # US announces tariffs on dozens of countries over forced labour concerns

![](https://static.files.bbci.co.uk/bbcdotcom/web/20260723-115353-11d20ce153-web-3.15.1-1/grey-placeholder.png)
![Getty Images President Donald Trump pointing his finger. He has a serious look on his face and is wearing a blue suit with a white shirt and red tie.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/news/480/cpsprodpb/02b7/live/fa2c0bc0-86b1-11f1-bb58-d3ffca85db6d.jpg.webp)

The US is imposing new tariffs on imports from around 60 trading partners over claims they failed to properly stop forced labour.

The duties, ranging from 10% to 12.5%, target key economic partners – including the UK, EU, Canada, Japan, and India. They are set to go into effect on Friday.

The move is the latest escalation in the global trade war which was reignited by US President Donald Trump when he returned to office in January last year.

It comes after the US Supreme Court ruled earlier this year that many of the tariffs imposed globally under emergency powers were illegally enacted. The president has since sought other legal avenues to push through his flagship trade policy.

Trump has used tariffs to create more US manufacturing jobs and boost the American economy. But he has also used them to press other countries, such as Mexico, on non-trade issues, such as labor rules.

The White House has singled out Canadian imports in recent days, warning that goods crossing the northern border will face 50% duties.
